human_review_notes: 5.3 uses more defensible, not guaranteed, for n=40 with a skewed population. 5.7/5.8 retain the worksheet n>=30 classroom CLT convention; precise tail accuracy for extreme skew would need further distribution information.

6.9 retains the familiar AP phrase students like these volunteers. Causal inference is supported for randomized participants; transport to other similar students needs a substantive similarity judgment and never implies all district students.
The 8--10 minute finish estimates are planning judgments, not observed student timing; pilot the longest condition-check days (6.2, 6.3, 6.8) with this class.
patterns: Several headings and one callout supplied the result students were meant to justify. Neutral headings preserve the need to adjudicate.
Many arguments combined a choice, repeated calculations, full interpretation, reader consequences, and another design task. Trimming extra tasks preserves the claim/evidence/reasoning demand.
Before-video prompts often requested terminology or a complete method judgment. Concrete one-sentence choices are more accessible.
Missing inputs and method requirements emerged only when checking against the actual worksheet: 5.8 population sizes, 6.8 critical value, and 6.11 one-sided confidence bounds.
